record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of non-uniform hyperbolicity
record.context_brief: Conjecture 4.4 specialized to the Katok map
record.original_question: For the Katok map, prove the local genericity statement of Conjecture 4.4: if the map has nonzero Lyapunov exponents almost everywhere, must there be an open neighbourhood in the volume-preserving C^{1+α} topology in which the maps with nonzero Lyapunov exponents on a set of positive measure form a residual subset?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.2. Prove Conjecture 4.4 for the Katok map.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The Katok map is a celebrated example of a C^∞ area-preserving diffeomorphism of the 2-torus T² (or, in a variant, of the 2-sphere with a suitable smooth area form), obtained by a smooth slow-down of a linear hyperbolic automorphism near a fixed point. It preserves Lebesgue (area) measure m, is ergodic with respect to m, and has nonzero Lyapunov exponents at m-almost every point.

Fix α ∈ (0,1) and consider Diff^{1+α}_m(M), the space of C^{1+α} diffeomorphisms of the underlying surface M preserving the smooth area form m, equipped with the C^{1+α} topology. Say that a diffeomorphism f ∈ Diff^{1+α}_m(M) "has nonzero Lyapunov exponents on a set of positive measure" if the set of points x ∈ M at which all Lyapunov exponents of f are nonzero has positive m-measure.

Question: Does there exist an open neighbourhood U ⊂ Diff^{1+α}_m(M) of the Katok map such that the set
   { f ∈ U : f has nonzero Lyapunov exponents on a set of positive m-measure }
is a residual subset of U (i.e. contains a dense G_δ subset of U)?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a proof of the local C^{1+α} genericity statement for the Katok map. Known related results concern the C^1 topology (Bochi–Mañé-type residuality, where zero exponents are typical), or constructions of robust nonzero exponents in special partially hyperbolic settings, none of which resolve the C^{1+α} local genericity question around the Katok example. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Lyapunov exponents of generic volume-preserving and symplectic maps
status_evidence.snippet: C^1-generic area-preserving diffeomorphisms are either Anosov or have zero Lyapunov exponents a.e.
status_evidence.claim: The C^1 picture is opposite to what is asked in C^{1+α}, and no C^{1+α} analogue near the Katok map is established.

status_evidence.title: Genericity of zero Lyapunov exponents
status_evidence.snippet: For C^1 area-preserving diffeomorphisms, residually one has zero exponents or Anosov.
status_evidence.claim: Available genericity results are in the C^1 topology, not the C^{1+α} topology relevant here.
